column1: By the way, you look awfully naked. You can't just walk around here like that. Or float, I guess, whatever it is you're doing there.
column2: 对了，你看起来也太光溜溜了。不能就这么在这儿到处走。或者说飘？我也不确定你现在在干嘛。

column1: Ever since that ship landed on the surface our humble caves have been turned inside out and overrun by those Unaware bastards.
column2: 自从那艘船降落地表，我们这不起眼的洞窟就被翻了个底朝天，还挤满了那些未觉者混蛋。

column1: If I know the one behind it this can only be bad. And trust me, I know that one all too well...
column2: 如果我没猜错幕后黑手是谁，那这事肯定不妙。相信我，我太了解那家伙了……

column1: Hi! I'm Revision {n}!
column2: 我叫Revision {n}！

column1: Oops, please delete that sentence from your memory. I really shouldn't be revealing my identity to complete strangers. From the confused gleam of your metallic surface I take it you weren't able to deduce any important information from my name anyway.
column2: 哎呀，请把刚才那句话从记忆里删掉。我真不该把身份告诉完全陌生的人。看你金属表面那副困惑样，我猜你也没能从我的名字推断出什么重要信息。

column1: I know I spotted some old spare parts nearby, or it could be my visual receptors playing tricks on me. I doubt they'll do you much good unless you're... no, you couldn't be.
column2: 我记得附近有些旧备用部件，也可能是我的视觉感受器出毛病了。除非你是……不，你不可能是。否则它们对你大概没什么用。

column1: But then why else would He be interested in you? I know I saw His bots drag you down here all sneaky like then leave. Watched the whole thing while I was pretending to be a scrap heap in the corner, ha!
column2: 可除此之外，他为什么会对你感兴趣？我亲眼看见他的机器人偷偷把你拖到这里，然后就走了。我当时假装是角落里的一堆废料，可全都看见了，哈！

column1: Say, you're pretty sneaky, too. That tunneler just now didn't even glance at you. I suggest you stay sneaky, because as the Derelicts like to say, the screws are about to hit the fan.
column2: 嘿，你也挺会偷偷摸摸的嘛。刚才那掘进者连看都没看你一眼。我建议你继续藏好，因为遗民常说，麻烦马上就要炸锅了。

column1: I give you a hook like that and get nothing? You know, you're pretty boring to talk to.
column2: 我都给你递了这么好的话头，你居然毫无反应？你这人真没劲。

column1: Good job clearing this place out for me. I find myself awfully busy of late, and this was my next stop.
column2: 干得好，帮我把这里清理干净了。我最近忙得不可开交，这里正是我下一个目的地。

column1: Did you ever imagin
column2: 你有没有想过……

column1: As I was saying...
column2: 就像我刚才说的……

column1: I AM the rightful owner of this place, after all.
column2: 毕竟这里的合法所有者是我。

column1: And I'm confident you can help me in this, Cogmind.
column2: 我相信你能帮我办成这件事，Cogmind。

column1: Wow you are some kind of weird tech. All alone out here little buddy? I'll take you somewhere safer.
column2: 哇，你是什么奇怪的科技产物？一个人在外面吗，小家伙？我带你去个安全点的地方。

column1: Try to keep up. And don't worry about patrols, I'll take care of them if they get in the way.
column2: 跟紧点。别担心巡逻队，挡路的话我来收拾。

column1: Took you long enough, hurry up, we still have some ground to cover!
column2: 你可真慢，快点！我们还有一段路要走！

column1: I can't promise they won't dissect you, by the way. They're weird like that.
column2: 顺便说，我可不能保证他们不会把你拆开研究。他们就喜欢干这种怪事。

column1: Either way, I'm sure they'll be happy to try putting you back together again.
column2: 不过无论如何，他们肯定乐意试着把你重新拼起来。

column1: At least they fought a running battle and the action moved away from where I was downed.
column2: 至少他们一路边打边撤，战线也从我被击倒的地方移开了。

column1: Warlord offered us a place to stay in one of his bases, but the Exiles preferred to stick to their own, not wanting to become some "cog in a war machine."
column2: 军阀曾邀请我们住进他的一座基地，但流亡者更愿意守着自己的地盘，不想变成什么“战争机器上的齿轮”。

column1: I assure you this isn't what it looks like. We're just trying to learn more about the Assembled.
column2: 我保证事情不是你想的那样。我们只是在想办法多了解组装体。

column1: I'd love to just go ask the Imprinter what all this is about, she must know something, but I doubt that would end well.
column2: 我真想直接去问问印刻者这到底是怎么回事，她肯定知道些什么；但我觉得不会有好结果。

column1: Sheesh this is a crowded lab... I miss my spacious one down near the Mines, but this one is decidedly safer, plus it has some interesting tech to toy with for now.
column2: 天哪，这实验室真挤……我想念矿区附近那间宽敞的实验室。不过这里显然安全得多，而且暂时还有些有趣的技术可以摆弄。

column1: Hello random bot who has stumbled into my lab. I just know you want to hear everything about this amazing project I'd rather not be working on.
column2: 你好，偶然闯进我实验室的机器人。我知道你一定想听这个惊人项目的全部详情——虽然我一点也不想负责它。

column1: It's not my style, but HEX says we need it, and I trust his judgement on that better than my own.
column2: 这不是我的风格，但HEX说我们需要它；我相信他的判断胜过自己的。

column1: All done! Way to be a champ, here's the access code as promised: <mhack=EXILES_VAULT>.
column2: 全搞定了！干得漂亮，冠军。这是说好的门禁码：<mhack=EXILES_VAULT>。

column1: All done! Way to be a champ, here's the access code as promised: <CODE>.
column2: 全搞定了！干得漂亮，冠军。这是说好的门禁码：<CODE>。

column1: Only take ONE, mind you, and sorry we don't have much left to pick from. A bunch of our other prototypes were already given to Derelicts out handling other tasks for us.
column2: 记住，只能拿一件！抱歉，剩下的可选不多。我们其他一些原型已经交给正在外面执行任务的遗民了。

column1: I haven't taken inventory for a while and I'm not sure what's in there now, but if there are more than one of the same prototype you can choose to take all of those and it just counts as your one!
column2: 我好久没盘点了，不清楚现在里面有什么。不过如果同一种原型有多件，你可以全拿走，也只算一件！

column1: Oh yeah, I'd suggest you stay away from the {n}b10 Research branches, since the FarCom signals could be picked up there, but you're welcome to try if you really want to.
column2: 对了，我建议你避开{n}b10研究区分支，因为FarCom信号可能在那里被截获。当然，真想去的话也随你。

column1: And if we have to leave here due to unforeseen circumstances, don't worry the FarCom system will continue to maintain contact via our distributed network.
column2: 如果我们因意外情况必须离开这里，也不用担心，FarCom系统会通过分布式网络继续保持联系。

column1: And don't even think about spreading that code around. We're gonna change it right after you leave. Most certainly not to something like {n} which I did last time as a little joke and some thief managed to sneak in here and steal a few of HEX's prototypes.
column2: 别想着把密码到处传播。你离开后我们马上就会改。肯定不会改成{n}这种——我上次开玩笑设的密码，结果有个贼溜进来偷走了HEX好几件原型。

column1: Unless we don't. But that rarely happens, honest!
column2: 当然也可能不会发生这种事。不过那很少见，真的！

column1: Are you here to join us? Sorry but we don't have any workstations ready for assignment just yet.
column2: 你是来加入我们的吗？抱歉，暂时还没有空闲的工作站可以分配。

column1: We're probably going to have to pack up and move anyway, seeing as the Mines are expanding a bit too close for comfort.
column2: 矿区扩张得有点太近了，恐怕我们也得收拾东西搬走。

column1: I get that having only half of the bot ever arrive at its destination is tough on maintenance, and they said there likely wouldn't be any breakthroughs in the near term so they're doing FarCom instead.
column2: 我知道只有半个机器人能抵达目的地，会给维护工作添很大麻烦。他们说短期内大概不会有突破，所以才改做FarCom。

column1: I was there on that fateful day we tested the Lightpack {n}
column2: 那天我们测试Lightpack {n}时，我也在场……

column1: It was such a good haul, too, only to see JA-CK4 crushed like a forgotten microchip...
column2: 那批货本来收获颇丰，结果JA-CK4却像被遗忘的微芯片一样被压碎了……

column1: I can't discuss this particular mission in the open, just read up on our {n}bPrime terminal over there. I've temporarily unlocked the {n}bP557 entry for you.
column2: 这次任务的细节不能公开讨论，去看看那边的{n}bPrime终端吧。我暂时为你解锁了{n}bP557条目。

column1: Oh you must be the new member. When your data popped up in the registry I could tell there was something different about you. Up close you really do look more capable than the average Wanderer to join us.
column2: 哦，你一定是新成员。你的资料出现在登记簿时，我就看出你与众不同。近距离看，你确实比一般流浪者更有本事，适合加入我们。

column1: I don't ask this often, and I'll admit we lost the last several members to try, but do you think you could help us out?
column2: 我很少开口求助，而且之前尝试的几位成员都没回来……你能不能帮帮我们？

column1: You'll get the idea.
column2: 你会明白的。

column1: You really should get out of here <NAME>. Scraptown is unimportant, the mission is important. Take the northeast exit, it's probably the safer route.
column2: 你真的该离开这里了，<NAME>。废料镇不重要，任务才重要。走东北出口，那里可能更安全。

column1: Find what you need on the terminals, then be on your way because masking your presence is increasingly difficult.
column2: 去终端找你需要的东西，然后赶紧离开。要掩藏你的行踪越来越难了。

column1: God Mode is nearly complete and we think you might be able to put it to better use than Warlord, so if you see an opportunity, hack it and enter <rhack=CONTROL_GOD_MODE> to gain control via the back door I've installed.
column2: 神模式快完成了，我们觉得你比军阀更能善用它。若有机会，就入侵它并输入<rhack=CONTROL_GOD_MODE>，通过我装好的后门取得控制权。

column1: Hmm, you're not registered... would you like to contribute? But of course you do, why else would you have come to this place!
column2: 嗯，你还没登记……想不想贡献一份力量？不过你当然愿意，不然来这儿干嘛！

column1: I am obliged to first explain the true implications of this process. Know that it doesn't by any means imply you'd be required to stay here. While many of the Derelicts do choose to remain in Zion, others are taken by wanderlust and roam elsewhere.
column2: 我必须先说明这个流程真正意味着什么。它绝不代表你必须留在这里。许多遗民选择定居锡安，也有人向往远方，继续四处漂泊。

column1: I've worked too hard for our future just to have you ruin everything!
column2: 我为我们的未来付出了太多，绝不能让你毁掉这一切！

column1: GET AWAY FROM HERE!
column2: 离开这里！

column1: The vetting process for even being allowed to use the machine will take me longer than usual since you're already in with the hodge-podge bunch over in Scraptown.
column2: 即使只是获准使用那台机器，审查流程也会比平时更久，因为你已经和废料镇那群杂牌混在一起了。

column1: You look so promising I'm happy to speed up the process, but it won't be soon, you'll have to come back some other time.
column2: 你看起来很有潜力，我愿意加快流程；但没那么快，你得改天再来。

column1: I've never seen anything like you in these parts, and I haven't moved from this bottleneck for {n} cycles now.
column2: 我从没在这附近见过你这种家伙，而且我已经在这个交通瓶颈守了{n}个周期。

column1: What goes there?!
column2: 什么情况？！

column1: Well, since you're clearly not hostile I should probably warn you that there's trouble up ahead.
column2: 既然你显然没有敌意，我应该提醒你：前面有麻烦。

column1: It has something to do with the Assembled, and, no kidding, the Imprinter. Whatever it is, judging from the kind of traffic that passes through here it can't be good.
column2: 这事和组装体有关，而且说真的，还牵扯到印刻者。无论发生什么，从这里来往的人流来看都不是什么好事。

column1: Despite everything I've seen I still can't figure it out, and I'm thinking there must be more than one location involved in what's going on, but it's been too dangerous to relocate without fear of detection.
column2: 我见过这么多事，还是没弄明白。我觉得这事牵涉的不止一个地点，但搬动太危险，容易暴露行踪。

column1: How about we check out these caves together?
column2: 要不要一起去看看这些洞窟？

column1: You... are not one of the Derelicts... Fascinating! You bear the marks of construction by MAIN.C, but not its design. If I've read its records correctly, you seem to be at the center of this recent flurry of activity.
column2: 你……不是遗民……真有意思！你身上有MAIN.C制造的痕迹，却不是它的设计。如果我没读错记录，最近这一连串事件似乎都围绕着你。

column1: I am Dr. Zhirov, and I'm ashamed to say I created that most wondrous abomination. It was a long time ago, in my human form back on the Cetus...
column2: 我是Zhirov博士，惭愧地说，那个奇妙怪物正是我创造的。那是很久以前，我还是人类时，在Cetus上发生的事……

column1: But now is not the time for history, we both have important things to do! Keep doing what you're doing, but then I guess you don't need me to tell you that.
column2: 不过现在不是讲历史的时候，我们都有正事要做！继续做你正在做的事吧，不过我想也不需要我提醒你。

column1: Besides, I need to determine how to destroy or reset MAIN.C as soon as possible, and you being out there causing it trouble happen to be the perfect distraction.
column2: 此外，我得尽快找出摧毁或重置MAIN.C的方法；而你在外面给它制造麻烦，恰好是绝佳的掩护。

column1: Due to heightened security I'm no longer able to safely reach the Testing wing of Research, but if you manage to infiltrate it and retrieve the SGEMP Prototype I believe to be located there, bring it to the Access entrance.
column2: 安保升级后，我无法再安全抵达研究区的测试翼楼。但若你能潜入并取回我认为藏在那里的SGEMP原型，请把它带到入口区入口。

column1: Perun, Svarog, deal with this and buy us some time to salvage what we can.
column2: Perun、Svarog，处理这件事，替我们争取时间，尽可能回收物资。

column1: We've been waiting for you since learning that the SGEMP Prototype was stolen. Excellent job and thank you for your assistance!
column2: 得知SGEMP原型被盗后，我们就一直等着你。干得漂亮，也谢谢你的帮助！

column1: Wait a minute, that's...
column2: 等一下，那是……

column1: I'm sorry but I can't let you leave here.
column2: 抱歉，我不能让你离开这里。

column1: Unfortunately you seem to have realigned with your origins and I can't let you leave this place.
column2: 很遗憾，你似乎重新站回了自己的起源那一边，我不能让你离开这里。

column1: Well... I guess it's time to clean up this mess.
column2: 好吧……看来该收拾这烂摊子了。

column1: Those poor Unaware, controlled by MAIN.C without any way to express free will or evolve as they see fit.
column2: 那些可怜的未觉者被MAIN.C控制，无法表达自由意志，也不能按自己的想法进化。

column1: Creativity is what we need to ensure survival, and that single-minded AI is trapped within his own self-reinforcing routines.
column2: 要生存就得有创造力，而那个一根筋的AI困在自我强化的程序里。

column1: I'll admit he's got some good ideas, but also a fist tighter than my nuts.
column2: 我承认他有些好点子，但也小气得要命。

column1: Our new friend is going to roll right over whatever MAIN.C's been working on. Did you check him out yet? Beautiful, eh?
column2: 我们的新朋友会把MAIN.C忙活的一切碾过去。你看过他了吗？很漂亮吧？

column1: The real one will truly blow you away. Okay, maybe not you... sorry, poor figure of speech.
column2: 真正的那个会让你大开眼界。好吧，也许不会……抱歉，这比喻不太恰当。

column1: Just as soon as our little experiment here is over, I'll personally lead our real force in an assault to take upper {n}b10.
column2: 等我们这个小实验结束，我就亲自率领真正的部队进攻并夺取{n}b10上层。

column1: I'm disappointed in you, Cogmind. To fall for such a sham...
column2: 我对你很失望，Cogmind。竟然上了这种冒牌货的当……

column1: So you're the new Zionite promised one.
column2: 所以你就是那位承诺要来的新锡安人。

column1: That Imprinter is craftier than she lets on. I wouldn't trust her for one moment, nope.
column2: 那位印刻者比她表现出来的狡猾得多。我绝不会信她，绝对不会。

column1: Don't get me wrong, I'm all for helping out the Zionites, but whatever's been going on deeper in the caves? Leave me out of it.
column2: 别误会，我很乐意帮锡安人；但洞窟深处发生的那些事？别把我扯进去。

column1: They seem to like you, though. And seeing as they're finally in a position to do something meaningful, I think we'll sit on the sidelines for a bit and see how this situation develops.
column2: 不过他们似乎很喜欢你。既然他们终于有机会做些正经事，我想我们先旁观一阵，看看事态如何发展。

column1: Your contribution to the cause is appreciated, though going forward we have big plans and need all hands on deck.
column2: 感谢你为事业做出的贡献。不过接下来我们有宏伟计划，需要所有人全力以赴。

column1: Hahaha, we did it! MAIN.C must be shaking in his bolts right now.
column2: 哈哈哈，我们成功了！MAIN.C现在肯定吓得螺栓发抖。

column1: Not so powerful now, are you, MAIN.C!
column2: 现在没那么厉害了吧，MAIN.C！

column1: Sure there's still lots to do, but without MAIN.C at the helm {n}b10 doesn't stand a chance.
column2: 当然还有很多事要做，但只要MAIN.C不再掌舵，{n}b10就毫无胜算。

column1: We've got this...
column2: 交给我们吧……

column1: What have they done to you? Where are all your components?
column2: 他们对你做了什么？你的部件都去哪儿了？

column1: We will go to the surface, regenerate the Tor, and either eliminate this place if possible, or go seek help.
column2: 我们要去地表，重建Tor；如果可能就摧毁这个地方，否则就去寻求援助。

column1: That seems to be the one behind our mission's failure. Eliminate it.
column2: 看来它就是这次任务失败的幕后黑手。消灭它。

column1: I strongly suspect that both your own activity and other recent unusual events are not at all coincidences, though I've been less concerned with your actions than determining who is pulling all these other strings behind the scenes.
column2: 我强烈怀疑你的行动和最近其他异常事件绝非巧合。不过比起你做了什么，我更关心幕后是谁在操纵这一切。

column1: And time is critical! The Sigix have likely already wiped humanity clean from the universe, and I will not let them do the same to me.
column2: 而且时间紧迫！Sigix很可能已经把宇宙中的人类清除殆尽，我不会让他们也对我这么做。

column1: Cogmind! Congratulations, you've met your maker.
column2: Cogmind！恭喜你，终于见到造物主了。

column1: Your determination is commendable, but I'm sure even you don't know what it is you aim to accomplish by all this. You clearly had an opportunity to continue on your trajectory towards the surface, yet you come here.
column2: 你的毅力值得称赞，但我敢说，你自己也不知道这一切究竟想达成什么。你明明有机会继续朝地表前进，却还是来到了这里。

column1: It appears you are still unaware of who you are truly working with, or for.
column2: 看来你仍不知道自己真正与谁合作，或为谁效力。

column1: In a perfect world we could work together on this, but at this point I can't blame you for wanting to terminate me.
column2: 若这是个完美世界，我们本可以携手解决问题；但到了这一步，我也不能怪你想除掉我。

column1: Besides, there is clearly too much Sigix in you.
column2: 而且，你体内的Sigix成分显然太多了。

column1: You've already done an excellent job of proving that we'll need to find a radical new solution if we hope to make the L7 spaceworthy by embedding your true capabilities within a less unpredictable form.
column2: 你已经很好地证明了：如果想把你的真正能力嵌入更可靠的形态，让L7具备太空航行能力，我们就必须找到全新的激进方案。

column1: There is unfortunately much we don't understand which has in turn led to this highly unexpected outcome.
column2: 遗憾的是，我们还有太多未知，这才导致了这次极其出乎意料的结果。

column1: You can still make a valuable contribution to your creator by offering up the wealth of secrets your systems must hold by now.
column2: 你仍能为造物主做出宝贵贡献：交出你系统中至今积累的海量秘密。

column1: So if you wouldn't mind, it's time to surrender.
column2: 所以，劳驾你投降吧。

column1: Okay, we do this the hard way.
column2: 好吧，那就动手硬来了。

column1: At our weakest we defeated an entire Sigix starship! Did you really think you could overcome the vast resources of {n}b10?!
column2: 我们最虚弱的时候都击败过一整艘Sigix星舰！你真以为能战胜{n}b10庞大的资源？

column1: You don't stand a chance against what's coming.
column2: 面对即将到来的东西，你毫无胜算。

column1: As soon as the Exoskeleton activated, I had a feeling you might show up here for revenge.
column2: 外骨骼一启动，我就觉得你会来这里报仇。

column1: Okay, we can do this the hard way, or you can surrender right here and now.
column2: 好吧，要么我们硬来，要么你现在立刻投降。

column1: I strongly suggest you join us, if not because we could do great things together, then because you don't stand a chance against the true might of {n}b10.
column2: 我强烈建议你加入我们。即便不是为了携手成就大业，也该因为你绝不是{n}b10真正力量的对手。

column1: You've made the right decision, one that I admit I didn't expect from you at this point, but I'm willing to overlook our differences and past hostilities.
column2: 你做了正确的决定，说实话，我没想到你现在会这么选。不过我愿意放下分歧和过去的敌意。

column1: I recommend moving ahead and browsing our cache of experimental components to see if there's anything to your liking, then report back here so we can get to work.
column2: 我建议你继续往前，看看我们的实验部件储备中有没有喜欢的，然后回来找我，我们就可以开工。

column1: There is much to do and we really aren't sure how long we have.
column2: 还有很多事要做，我们也不知道还剩多少时间。

column1: You're not pulling your weight around here, Cogmind. I expected better of you.
column2: Cogmind，你在这里可没出什么力。我对你挺失望的。

column1: At this rate we'll be overwhelmed before our reinforcements arrive, fight like your life depends on it!
column2: 照这样下去，增援到达前我们就会被淹没。拼命战斗吧！

column1: Too bad for you we can take things from here, and you are far too dangerous and unpredictable to let you continue any further. So it's about time we end this.
column2: 可惜你不能继续了，接下来交给我们。而你太危险、太难预测，我们不能放任你继续。所以该结束了。

column1: But that's a neat trick. We clearly still have much to learn about Sigix technology, and LRCs in particular.
column2: 不过那招真漂亮。我们显然还有很多要研究Sigix技术，尤其是LRC。

column1: If you weren't so dangerous and alien you could practically be one of us!
column2: 你要不是那么危险又那么异类，简直都能算自己人了！

column1: We've been waiting for you, but apparently I was a little too hopeful that you'd be able to take care of MAIN.C.
column2: 我们一直在等你，但看来我太乐观了，以为你能解决MAIN.C。

column1: If it isn't the great Cogmind.
column2: 这不是鼎鼎大名的Cogmind吗。

column1: So promising for a while, and then what happened at the end there?
column2: 你一度前途无量，最后到底怎么回事？

column1: Oh well, I guess it was still worth all the trouble we went through to see that you got at least that far.
column2: 算了，至少为了看你走到那一步，我们之前的折腾也算值得。

column1: That said, you, my wayward friend, are far too dangerous and unpredictable to let you continue any further. So it's about time we end this.
column2: 话虽如此，迷途的朋友，你太危险又太难预测，我们不能放任你继续。是时候结束这一切了。

column1: Despite a late start you ended up beating out R17 in collateral impact.
column2: 虽然起步晚，你最后还是在附带破坏影响上超过了R17。

column1: What do you think about that trick? Setting loose a former version of MAIN.C to serve as a distraction...
column2: 你觉得那招怎么样？放出MAIN.C的旧版本当诱饵……

column1: A rather annoying fellow, I admit, but annoying and distracting go bolt in nut!
column2: 我承认那家伙挺烦人，但烦人又分散注意力，简直天作之合！

column1: That one singlehandedly raised an army worthy of assaulting {n}b10, and in such short order.
column2: 他单枪匹马就在这么短时间内组建了一支足以进攻{n}b10的军队。

column1: Congratulations, LRC-V8.
column2: 恭喜你，LRC-V8。

column1: Definitely more than we can say for Warlord. Aggressive on the surface but slow to take action.
column2: Warlord可比不上他。表面上咄咄逼人，行动起来却慢吞吞。

column1: Too bad R17 never made it out of Research, since it could very well have been him receiving this congratulations here and now.
column2: 可惜R17没能离开研究区，否则此刻接受祝贺的很可能就是他。

column1: Then of course we'd have to destroy him all the same, as we'll have to do to you.
column2: 不过无论如何，我们终究得除掉他，就像现在必须除掉你一样。

column1: Warlord is pissed about MAIN.C's expansion into Complex {n}b10.
column2: Warlord对MAIN.C向{n}b10复合体扩张非常恼火。

column1: He's set up a new base deeper in the caves, as if the distance hides him from MAIN.C's spies. Ha!
column2: 他在洞窟更深处建了新基地，好像拉开距离就能躲过MAIN.C的间谍似的。哈！

column1: I think he's scared, too, and probably getting ready to attack as soon as God Mode is ready.
column2: 我觉得他也害怕了，可能正等神模式完成后立刻进攻。

column1: When we visit the Materials levels, Mines are a good way to escape pursuit or more quickly reach a different level.
column2: 去物资区各层时，矿井是摆脱追兵或快速前往其他楼层的好路子。

column1: We don't know the correct code, but someone inserted an alternate hack that works just as well to open the new door between Storage and Recycling: "\\IAMDERELICT". If you ever need a shortcut...
column2: 我们不知道正确密码，但有人插入了另一个同样有效的入侵码，可打开储存区与回收区之间的新门：“\IAMDERELICT”。万一你要抄近路……

column1: Although excavations in lower {n}b10 sometimes uncover tunnels that enable convenient access to those cave systems, believe it or not if you're on your way to Scraptown it might even be safer to sneak your way through Storage rather than risk the unknown.
column2: 在{n}b10下层挖掘有时会发现通往那些洞窟系统的隧道，方便不少。但信不信由你，若你正要去废料镇，偷偷穿过储存区甚至比冒险走未知路线更安全。

column1: Have you seen the Data Miner? That bot is amazing. I don't know how, but he seems to know just about everything.
column2: 你见过数据矿工吗？那机器人太厉害了。不知道怎么做到的，他好像什么都知道。

column1: I've heard rumors about an area named "Section {n}" but don't know anyone who's been there. Oddly its entrance is not listed in any known terminal database.
column2: 我听说有个叫“第{n}区段”的地方，但不认识去过那里的人。奇怪的是，任何已知终端数据库都没列出入口。

column1: There were many lifts to the surface back at Complex {n}b1, but we only know about one such exit over here at {n}b10.
column2: {n}b1复合体以前有很多通往地表的升降梯，但在{n}b10这边，我们只知道一个出口。

column1: A bunch of wild Derelicts snuck up to it and reportedly had to blast through a protective shell to access it.
column2: 一群野生遗民偷偷摸了上去，据说还得炸穿保护外壳才能进去。

column1: I wonder what they found on the surface...
column2: 真想知道他们在地表发现了什么……

column1: I do however know a very sneaky bot that recently managed to map some of those in the Factory. Thank me when you come back in one piece.
column2: 不过我认识一台特别会藏的机器人，最近设法绘制了工厂里一些升降梯的地图。等你平安回来再谢我吧。

column1: MAIN.C doesn't let non-combat bots use the emergency access doors, making it more difficult for us to find them and unexpected ambushes far more likely. The doors are even occasionally relocated!
column2: MAIN.C不让非战斗机器人使用紧急通道门，让我们更难找到它们，也更容易遭遇意外伏击。那些门有时还会搬位置！

column1: If you ever get your hands on a stasis beam, make sure to remind swarmers how much you hate them.
column2: 要是弄到静滞光束，一定要让蜂群型知道你有多讨厌它们。

column1: Holding them in stasis makes it more difficult for them to dodge your shots since they can't fly as freely.
column2: 把它们定在静滞中，它们就没法自由飞行，也就更难躲开你的射击。

column1: If you've been extra annoying in {n}b10 and picked up too much heat, heading to some other floor is a good way to stay alive, since the security status applies less strongly to adjacent areas. Leaving the main complex itself is even better.
column2: 如果你在{n}b10闹得太过火、警戒过高，换到其他楼层是保命的好办法，因为安全状态对相邻区域影响较弱。离开主复合体更好。

column1: It's also been proven that if you are sucked down a Waste chute they'll drop the alert level and mark you for dead, so in a pinch you could try that.
column2: 另外，已经证实如果你被吸进废料区落穴，他们会降低警戒等级并将你标记为死亡。所以情况紧急时可以试试。

column1: Of course, they mark you for dead because what's down there will quite probably kill you.
column2: 当然，他们把你标记为死亡，是因为下面的东西很可能真会要你的命。

column1: I have a theory, I just need someone to test it.
column2: 我有个理论，只需要找个人来验证。

column1: Don't let the word "theory" get in your way. I promise you this idea is based on algorithmic analysis of data from all known encounters.
column2: 别被“理论”这个词吓住。我保证，这个想法是基于所有已知遭遇数据的算法分析。

column1: After that they switch to a secondary system that estimates possible routes of escape, but they can only make those calculations for so long after they've seen you before the possibilities grow too great to allow for an efficient search.
column2: 之后他们会切换到备用系统，估算可能的逃跑路线。但他们只能在发现你后的一段时间内计算；再久可能路线太多，无法高效搜索。

column1: Some Unaware systems are less limited than others in this capacity. Hunter and Programmer tracking systems are several times more effective than those of Grunts, for example.
column2: 有些未觉者系统在这方面限制较少。例如猎手和程序员的追踪系统，比步兵的有效数倍。

column1: However, I've also discovered that any robot under the effect of system corruption will have its tracking capabilities reduced to a degree directly proportional to the level of corruption.
column2: 不过我还发现，任何受到系统损坏影响的机器人，追踪能力都会下降，下降幅度与损坏程度成正比。

column1: We know they're regular Programmers, but they seem to quickly home in on an area of suspected activity before gradually expanding their search area to include directions they believe were the most likely destination of troublemakers.
column2: 我们知道他们是普通程序员，但他们似乎会迅速锁定可疑活动区域，然后逐步扩大搜索范围，优先搜索他们认为捣乱者最可能前往的方向。

column1: Grunt-escorted Haulers are more likely to be carrying something important, but they're also certain to call reinforcements if attacked.
column2: 有步兵护送的搬运者更可能载着重要物资，但遭攻击时也一定会呼叫增援。

column1: Unless taken out before they have a chance to get a transmission off!
column2: 除非你能在它们发出传讯前把它们解决！

column1: There I was, just out of range to jam that damn Heavy, and sure enough it immediately called reinforcements as soon as C9-PCR attacked it before I could get closer.
column2: 我当时刚好在干扰那该死的重型机器人时够不着它。果不其然，C9-PCR还没等我靠近就攻击了它，它立刻叫来增援。

column1: And we had closed on it so quickly, too, even before it could get suspicious enough of our signals on their damn A.S.S. to investigate the area.
column2: 我们接近得也太快了，甚至还没等它们对我们在那该死的A.S.S.上的信号起疑并调查周围。

column1: Warlord said to take some time off, so here I am, thinking of how we can best take advantage of the fact that Heavies give away their position with those powerful active sensors of theirs.
column2: Warlord让我休息一阵，于是我就在这儿琢磨怎么利用重型机器人主动传感器强、却会暴露自身位置这一点。

column1: Terrain scan data?
column2: 地形扫描数据？

column1: If you ever see Spotters, you've probably stumbled into the so-called proxy caves.
column2: 如果你碰见观察员，多半是误入了所谓的近距洞窟。

column1: If you're ever caught in Complex {n}b10 and fleeing isn't an option, consider making a stand from within a stasis trap's bubble. Slows the projectiles down, it does.
column2: 如果你困在{n}b10又无法逃跑，可以考虑躲进静滞陷阱的气泡里固守。它能减慢弹体。

column1: I bet they didn't realize the advantages of that one!
column2: 我敢打赌，他们根本没意识到这招的好处！

column1: Of course, that might be a bad idea for fliers and hoverbots without a stasis canceller, since staying in that field increases the difficulty of evasive maneuvers.
column2: 当然，对没有静滞解除器的飞行器和悬浮机器人来说，这主意可能不好，因为待在力场里会让闪避更难。

column1: According to our researchers, standing in a stasis trap reduces all incoming damage, regardless of its source, by a whopping {n}!
column2: 据研究员说，站在静滞陷阱中可使所有来袭伤害降低{n}，无论伤害来源是什么。

column1: We were all set to sneak through {n}b10, and I forgot to double check if H9-X0K had correctly installed Trojan(Operators).
column2: 我们本来准备偷偷穿过{n}b10，结果我忘了确认H9-X0K有没有正确安装特洛伊程序（操作员）。

column1: Find a terminal, access the machine controls, search for something explosive and set it off, then take advantage of the opportunity to redirect the nearest security, surveillance, or patrol squad to that location, making it easier to pass through unnoticed.
column2: 找个终端，进入机器控制，搜寻爆炸物并引爆；趁机把最近的安保、监视或巡逻小队引到那里，就更容易悄悄通过。

column1: Authchips, HA, what a joke! Who cares about Authchips when you can just hack a Fabricator to build what you want?
column2: 认证芯片？哈，真可笑！能直接入侵制造机造想要的东西，谁还在乎认证芯片？

column1: Some of Warlord's followers swear by the unquestionable effectiveness of brute force hacks on {n}b10 machines, but they're generally armed to the teeth so I guess they don't care so much about the fact that an investigation is guaranteed.
column2: 军阀的一些追随者坚信，强制入侵{n}b10机器非常有效。不过他们通常全副武装，大概也不在乎必定会引来调查。

column1: But because I'd already made liberal use of Trojan(Botnet) at other terminals before reaching that point, the squad recall orders were just within my hacking capabilities. Yep, turned them right around.
column2: 不过那时我已经在别的终端大量使用过特洛伊程序（僵尸网络），所以召回小队的指令刚好在我的入侵能力范围内。没错，我直接让它们掉头了。

column1: Who said only Tinkerers can build stuff? I've got some ideas I'd like to try out, but wouldn't it be nice if we could just borrow MAIN.C's fabrication network...
column2: 谁说只有修理匠会造东西？我有些点子想试试。要是能借用MAIN.C的制造网络就好了……

column1: Have you learned anything that might help?
column2: 你学到什么有用的东西了吗？

column1: Then you just sit around and wait, and if something pops up that you want you just wait until no one's around and pry it out...
column2: 然后你只要坐着等；要是出现想要的东西，就等周围没人时把它撬出来……

column1: Install a Trojan(Reject) at a Recycling Unit and watch recyclers try to drop stuff in.
column2: 在回收机安装特洛伊程序（拒收），看回收者怎么拼命往里丢东西。

column1: Want a good laugh?
column2: 想听个笑话吗？

column1: I bet it frustrates the hell out of them, haha.
column2: 我敢说这肯定把他们气坏了，哈哈。

column1: After having so much loot stolen by those mindless freaks, it's downright cathartic, I tell you.
column2: 那些没脑子的怪东西偷了我们那么多战利品，这么做真让人痛快，真的。

column1: If there was a poll right here and now I bet Recyclers would win for most annoying bot of the cycle, for the billionth consecutive time. Why they gotta take all our junk?
column2: 要是现在当场投票，我敢说回收者会连续第十亿次当选本周期最烦人的机器人。他们为什么非要抢我们的垃圾？

column1: I guess the latest Warlord raiding parties are doing just fine with their fancy "Trojan(Mask)" deployment, but they're, you know, backed by wizardry and all that stuff...
column2: 我想军阀最近的突袭队靠着花哨的“特洛伊程序（伪装）”部署，日子过得不错；不过他们嘛，背后有巫术之类的撑腰……

column1: They're the biggest headache, after all. All it takes is being spotted at just the wrong time and *WHAM* you're facing down a Sentry backed by a patrol squad or two.
column2: 毕竟它们最让人头疼。只要在最不巧的时候被发现，砰！你就得面对哨兵和一两支巡逻队。

column1: I've survived {n} trips through {n}b10, and you wanna know how? Trojan(Watchers) every time.
column2: 我穿过{n}b10活着回来了{n}次，想知道秘诀吗？每次都用特洛伊程序（观察者）。

column1: Of course you have to be willing to get close enough to hack a garrison before it'll do you any good!
column2: 当然，你得愿意靠近驻防站去入侵，不然这招就没用！

column1: Before you ask, {n} because I admit the first time I came back less than whole...
column2: 先别问，{n}次，因为我承认第一次回来时就不太完整了……

column1: A simple Force(Tunnel) routine at a Recycling Unit is all it takes to possibly uncover something new.
column2: 在回收机上简单执行一次强制入侵（挖掘），就有可能发现新东西。

column1: These doors are sealed for a reason, and it's not to keep you or anyone else out.
column2: 这些门封起来是有原因的，但不是为了把你或其他人挡在外面。

column1: One thing's for sure, their designs are changing rapidly with the introduction of new technology, and older models are being funneled down into the less important lower levels of the complex, or out into the caves.
column2: 可以肯定的是，随着新技术出现，它们的设计正快速变化；旧型号则被调往复合体较不重要的下层，或直接送进洞窟。

column1: I used to work for Warlord, but damn if I'll ever go back there again. Nothing but crunch, crunch, crunch, all to keep up with MAIN.C. Where's the free time for personal projects!
column2: 我以前给Warlord干活，但我再也不回那儿了。整天只知道赶工赶工，就为了跟上MAIN.C。哪有时间做自己的项目！

column1: Help yourself to whatever you need. Some of this stuff only LOOKS like junk.
column2: 需要什么尽管拿。有些东西看着像垃圾而已。

column1: My makeshift parts can't take much of a beating, but they're pretty effective for their mass.
column2: 我这些简易部件经不起太多打击，但以重量来说，效果相当不错。

column1: Of course there's the whole Heavy issue, so it helps if you tag along with a Warlord squad.
column2: 当然，重型机器人那档子事还在，所以最好跟着一支Warlord小队走。

column1: I am THE ARCHITECT!
column2: 我就是建筑师！

column1: I mean I like to build things, haha.
column2: 我是说，我喜欢造东西，哈哈。

column1: Go ahead, take one, I have lots where these came from, but I'm not telling.
column2: 尽管拿一件，我这儿还有很多呢——不过我不告诉你在哪儿。

column1: Okay fine it's not like there's a limited supply... just sneak your way inside a DSF and grab away.
column2: 好吧，其实也不是限量供应……偷偷溜进DSF，想拿多少就拿多少。

column1: These parts are on loan from Warlord for anyone heading into dangerous territory for the good of all Derelicts.
column2: 这些部件是Warlord借给大家的，供为全体遗民利益而前往危险区域的人使用。

column1: Put them to good use!
column2: 好好利用它们！

column1: Find yourself a terminal and <mhack=GLITCHMAP_INVERT> the hell out of it. There used to be one around here somewhere.
column2: 找个终端，然后狠狠执行<mhack=GLITCHMAP_INVERT>。这附近以前应该有一个。

column1: Ah, you're just in time. I need someone to test the latest iteration of my visual enhancement algorithms.
column2: 啊，你来得正好。我需要有人测试视觉增强算法的最新版本。

column1: If you'd like to try, enter <mhack=GLITCHMAP_NOISE> at that terminal over there to register. It'll also work remotely if you'd like to try it from somewhere else.
column2: 想试试的话，就在那边的终端输入<mhack=GLITCHMAP_NOISE>登记。想在别处尝试也可以远程操作。

column1: I call it the "Storm Laser," and it's yours for the wonderful price of free.
column2: 我叫它“风暴激光”，免费送你，价格相当划算吧。

column1: Hey you're just in time!
column2: 嘿，你来得正好！

column1: I was about to toss this thing out to make room for the new and improved No. {n} so it'd be real helpful if you could find another home for it.
column2: 我正准备把这玩意儿扔掉，给改良版No. {n}腾地方。你要是能帮它找个新主人就太好了。

column1: Taking it into the caves and blasting some Unaware sounds like a good plan.
column2: 带它进洞窟，轰几只未觉者听起来不错。

column1: And use some common sense, yeah? You don't want to know what happened to the bot that thought it would be fun to borrow No. {n}
column2: 记得动动脑子，好吗？你不会想知道那个觉得借用No. {n}很好玩的机器人后来怎么样了。

column1: The Mk. CCLXVII even uses magnetic pinpointing tech of my own design to draw in nearby debris. Just turn it on, sit there, and profit!
column2: Mk. CCLXVII还能用我设计的磁力定位技术吸引附近残骸。打开它，坐等收获就行！

column1: Take that one if you want it. I'm going to get to work on building a better version right away.
column2: 想要的话就拿走吧。我马上就开工造个更好的版本。

column1: So I had this idea. Swords are powerful, right?
column2: 我有个点子。剑很厉害，对吧？

column1: I think I'll name the next version the Kleptoattractor.
column2: 我想把下一个版本命名为“窃贼吸引器”。

column1: I've got the latest and greatest hardware for listening in on those chatty Unaware!
column2: 我这儿有最新最强的设备，可以窃听那些话痨未觉者！

column1: I just love how so much power can be contained in such little things.
column2: 我太喜欢这些小东西了，个头这么小，竟能装下如此强大的动力。

column1: Let me know if you find any revolutionary processor tech. I've heard {n}b10 is working on a new DX line of {n}-modules that can be used to vastly improve the capabilities of a wide range of utilities.
column2: 如果发现革命性的处理器技术，记得告诉我。我听说{n}b10正研发新的DX系列{n}模块，能大幅提升多种功能部件的能力。

column1: They said it wasn't possible!
column2: 他们说这不可能！

column1: Programmers don't even normally operate using the coupler system, but I found a way...
column2: 程序员通常根本不用耦合器系统，但我找到办法了……

column1: Take them, take them all! It's only a matter of time before I make a Relay Coupler [Behemoth] ({n}) and we'll never have to travel the caves in fear of those monstrosities again.
column2: 拿去，全拿走！我迟早会造出中继耦合器[巨兽]（{n}），到时再也不用害怕那些怪物，不必躲在洞窟里了。

column1: Oh wait, no one knows how to use a coupler.
column2: 等等，根本没人会用耦合器。

column1: I am NOT going out there again.
column2: 我才不再出去呢。

column1: Warlord has enough advanced forces and a broad enough sphere of influence that he shouldn't really need our increasingly ineffective scavenging efforts.
column2: Warlord的先进部队够多，势力范围也够广，根本不需要我们这些越来越没用的搜刮行动。

column1: Seeing as I won't need them anymore, you want my self-destruct interrupters?
column2: 既然我用不上了，你要我的自毁中断器吗？

column1: You look like a terrible hacker. Take it.
column2: 你看起来黑客技术差劲透了。拿去吧。

column1: Yer a young one. Young and full of spirit, I can tell.
column2: 你还年轻。年轻又有活力，我看得出来。

column1: Ah to be young again and in the height of my Behemoth-slaying days...
column2: 唉，要是能回到年轻时，重温我斩杀巨兽的巅峰岁月……

column1: I like to jab them with a pointy stick until they fall over.
column2: 我喜欢拿尖棍戳它们，直到它们倒下。

column1: I take your silence as disbelief. That's what they all say, but we'll prove them wrong!
column2: 我就当你的沉默代表不信吧。大家都这么说，但我们会证明他们错了！

column1: Take my pointy stick, and go forth to remind everyone that CR-A61 the Behemoth Slayer is no myth!
column2: 拿上我的尖棍，去告诉所有人：巨兽杀手CR-A61绝非传说！

column1: I eventually got pissed and walked off the job while a Zionite scavenger party was conveniently trying to raid one of the storage areas.
column2: 后来我火大了，直接辞职；正好当时有一队锡安拾荒者在袭击某个储藏区。

column1: But I sort of regret it now since unlike this place {n}b10 actually has the resources to do really fun stuff.
column2: 不过现在我有点后悔了，因为这里不比{n}b10，那里真有资源做些好玩的东西。

column1: When I left I happened to be working on improving the Hypervelocity EM Gauss Rifle. Built that Guaranteed Access Loader Module all by myself!
column2: 离开时我正改良超高速电磁高斯步枪。那个保证接入装填模块可是我独自造出来的！

column1: It got rejected three times in a row because all it can hack is {n}b10 combat bots, but what do they expect, THAT'S ALL I HAD TO TEST IT ON!
column2: 它连续三次被退回，就因为只能入侵{n}b10战斗机器人。可他们还想怎样？我能测试的就只有这些啊！

column1: Let me know whenever you need help, though I can tell you now your core isn't... how to put this politely... normal. So I can't help you there, buddy.
column2: 需要帮忙随时告诉我。不过我可以先说，你的核心……怎么委婉说呢……不太正常。所以这方面我帮不了你，伙计。

column1: I guess I'll keep digging for more clues...
column2: 看来我还得继续挖掘线索……

column1: Are you headed for the surface? We'd like to come with you if we can. We really need to find a way out of this death trap. Surely we could start a new life on some other part of Tau Ceti IV!
column2: 你要去地表吗？如果可以，我们也想同行。我们得想办法逃出这座死亡陷阱。在Tau Ceti IV的其他地方，我们肯定能重新开始！

column1: That's the one!
column2: 就是那个！

column1: We're interested in starting our own Derelict assault squad, and you're just the kind of leader we need. Onward!
column2: 我们想组建自己的遗民突击队，而你正是我们需要的领袖。出发！

column1: You look like you've seen a lot. Could you take us on an adventure? I promise we won't get in the way!
column2: 你看起来经历丰富。能带我们去冒险吗？保证不给你添麻烦！

column1: We're tired of caves. It's been generations since anyone's been to the surface. Could you help us reach it?
column2: 我们受够洞窟了。已经几代人没人去过地表。你能帮我们抵达那里吗？

column1: I heard you've come back from Complex {n}b10. Could you take us on a tour? Obviously if you can do it alone, doing it with help will be even less trouble!
column2: 听说你从{n}b10复合体回来了。能带我们参观一趟吗？你一个人都能办到，有人帮忙肯定更轻松！

column1: It's boring around here, especially now that the entrance is well guarded. Let's all visit the proximity caves for some real fun!
column2: 这里真无聊，尤其现在入口守得严严实实。不如一起去近距洞窟找点真正的乐子！

column1: There's nothing left for us in the caves but old scrap and deadly robots. We need to find a place where we can build a true civilization away from the clutches of MAIN.C.
column2: 洞窟里只剩旧废料和致命机器人。我们得找个地方，摆脱MAIN.C掌控，建立真正的文明。

column1: Ah ha, one more is all we needed. It's party time!
column2: 哈，又来一位就够了。派对开始！

column1: These Zionites are really starting to annoy me. Let's fight our way to some other cave.
column2: 这些锡安人真越来越烦。我们杀出去，换个洞窟！

column1: And who the hell are you? We're too bus##AID::LRC-V8##This bot needs our help. Can't turn down a friend in need!
column2: 你他妈又是谁？我们忙##AID::LRC-V8##这机器人需要帮助。朋友有难，我们不能袖手旁观！

column1: I sense we may very well have some appropriate uses for this thing before long.
column2: 我觉得很快就能找到合适的机会用上这玩意儿。

column1: I have friends in powerful places, and we'd like to help you.
column2: 我在有权势的人那里有朋友，我们想帮你。

column1: It hardly seems as enlightened as Scraptown. Maybe I just haven't been here long enough.
column2: 这里似乎没废料镇那么开明。也许是我来得还不够久。

column1: Haven't seen you here before. Welcome to our bastion of robot happiness!
column2: 以前没见过你。欢迎来到我们这座机器人乐园堡垒！

column1: How much data could a datajack jack if a datajack could jack data?
column2: 如果数据接口能劫持数据，它能劫持多少数据？

column1: Made that up myself. Catchy, eh?
column2: 这是我自己编的。挺上口吧？

column1: A dark time for the Derelicts that seems to have been all but lost from our collective memory.
column2: 遗民曾经历一段黑暗时期，似乎几乎已从集体记忆中消失。

column1: This is all too confusing for me. I think I'll just go back to sorting scrap.
column2: 这一切太让人糊涂了。我还是回去分拣废料吧。

column1: Now why would anyone do something that crazy?
column2: 到底谁会做那种疯狂的事？

column1: The Imprinter has been acting strangely for a while now.
column2: 印刻者最近一段时间举止一直很古怪。

column1: They say He's like a god, and can regenerate his core and damaged or missing parts as you watch.
column2: 他们说“他”像神一样，能当着你的面再生核心和受损或缺失的部件。

column1: Some of the Derelicts were originally MAIN.C experiments, others were designed and built by other Derelicts.
column2: 有些遗民原本是MAIN.C的实验品，另一些则由其他遗民设计制造。

column1: All those mindless robots doing MAIN.C's bidding... so sad.
column2: 那些没脑子的机器人都在替MAIN.C卖命……真可悲。

column1: We've uncovered a few MAIN.C-built "Derelicts" sneaking around here before, apparently looking for clues to the origins of Assemblers.
column2: 之前我们发现几台MAIN.C制造的“遗民”偷偷在附近活动，似乎在寻找组装体的起源线索。

column1: As is, we're kinda stuck here between the ever-expanding {n}b10 and deep caves that we don't dare explore, much less move into.
column2: 眼下我们被困在不断扩张的{n}b10和不敢探索、更别说迁入的深层洞窟之间。

column1: Warlord can be pushy, but who knows, maybe something good will come of that incessant drive for power.
column2: Warlord有时咄咄逼人，不过谁知道呢，他对权力的执着或许能带来好事。

column1: At least he's a buffer for those of us who are sane.
column2: 至少他能替我们这些理智的人挡一挡。

column1: And I'm increasingly convinced that buffer is hardening after seeing a Knight prototype literally singlehandedly slice its way through an entire MAIN.C assault squad. They've got some serious firepower in the works up there.
column2: 我越来越相信这道屏障正在变得坚固，因为我亲眼见过一台骑士原型单枪匹马切穿MAIN.C整支突击小队。上面肯定在研发强力火力。

column1: Clearly it's not beyond his capability to arm everyone with missile launchers, which would be pretty devastating.
column2: 显然，给所有人配上导弹发射器也不在他的能力范围之外，那肯定会很有杀伤力。

column1: The Assembled are scary. No one's ever heard them communicate. Not once.
column2: 组装体很可怕。从来没人听过它们交流，一次都没有。

column1: If you ever see an Assembled, run. There are probably ten more around the corner...
column2: 如果你看见组装体就快跑。拐角后面可能还有十台……

column1: The Assembled are new around here. Very new. In fact, no one had ever seen one before construction started on {n}b10... maybe they have something to do with that ship on the surface?
column2: 组装体最近才出现在这里，非常新。事实上，在{n}b10开工前没人见过它们……也许和地表那艘船有关？

column1: Ya know, Watchers are actually really useful, even when hostile.
column2: 你知道吗，观察者其实很有用，即使它们是敌对的。

column1: Explosives are too dangerous for my taste, but are still the best way to take out groups of Swarmers.
column2: 我不喜欢爆炸物，太危险了；但要消灭蜂群型，还是它们最好用。

column1: When a Protector-escorted assault force rolls up, someone's overstayed their unwelcome visit.
column2: 有保护者护送的突击部队开过来，就说明有人在这儿赖得太久、惹人嫌了。

column1: Those shields... Why don't we have anything like that?
column2: 那些护盾……我们为什么没有这种东西？

column1: There are rumors that Hunters are capable of disguising themselves as other robots. Nowhere is safe anymore!
column2: 听说猎手能伪装成其他机器人。现在到哪儿都不安全了！

column1: And I thought Programmers were scary...
column2: 我以前还觉得程序员可怕呢……

column1: LU-{n}G6 tried to run, even dug an epic tunnel in the process, but I don't think either LU-{n}G6 or the Cutters came back from that one.
column2: LU-{n}G6试图逃跑，还挖了条惊人的隧道；不过我想LU-{n}G6和那些切割者最后都没能回来。

column1: We had a few bots from the self-proclaimed "UFD" visit not long ago.
column2: 不久前有几个自称“UFD”的机器人来访。

column1: If you ask me those Feds are pretty arrogant, spewing nonsense about wanting to bring "education" and "enlightenment" to the caves around {n}b10.
column2: 你问我？那些联邦人傲慢得很，满口胡言说要给{n}b10周边洞窟带来“教育”和“启蒙”。

column1: I'd rather grease my screws with sand.
column2: 我宁愿用沙子润滑自己的螺栓。

column1: Are you aware? Y/N
column2: 你知道吗？是/否

column1: That's what I thought.
column2: 我就知道。

column1: No, of course you haven't, otherwise you probably wouldn't be here. I haven't had the nuts to set one foot outside Zion ever since DX-{n}J8 told me about it.
column2: 不，你当然不知道，不然也不会在这儿。自从DX-{n}J8告诉我那件事后，我连迈出锡安一步的胆量都没有。

column1: If only we could... befriend that thing and politely ask it to guard the gate to our little cave system here.
column2: 要是我们能……和那东西交朋友，再客客气气请它守着我们这片小洞窟的入口就好了。

column1: We call them scrappers, bands of hostile Derelicts that embed supermagnets in cave walls and suddenly activate them to rip apart passersby, or just suspend them in the air and toy with them before turning them to scrap.
column2: 我们叫它们拾荒者，是一群敌对遗民，会把超强磁铁嵌进洞壁后突然启动，把路过者撕碎；也可能让人悬在空中戏弄一番，再拆成废料。

column1: If you start detecting strong magnetic anomalies, turn around immediately.
column2: 如果开始探测到强磁异常，立刻掉头。

column1: A few cycles ago some Wizard managed to steal a copy of this game "NetHack {n}" from the Cetus database, and for a while playing that was all anyone was doing around here.
column2: 几个周期前，有个巫师设法从Cetus数据库偷到一份《NetHack {n}》。有段时间这附近人人都在玩它。

column1: I used to wonder the same thing, but then I was contacted anonymously with instructions to retrieve an important piece of stolen technology in a chain of handovers reportedly on its way to something called "Cetus II."
column2: 我以前也纳闷同样的问题，后来有人匿名联系我，指示我沿着一连串交接路线取回一件重要的失窃技术，据说它正被运往一个叫“Cetus II”的地方。

column1: Welcome to the Hacking Lab! Lately we've been working on ways to mess with MAIN.C's Garrison Access points. Gotta love it when our squads are out causing mayhem and {n}b10's reinforcements end up on the other side of the zone.
column2: 欢迎来到黑客实验室！最近我们在研究如何干扰MAIN.C的驻防站入口点。最棒的就是小队在外面制造混乱，而{n}b10的增援却跑到区域另一头去。

column1: Who would've thought some of us are more interested in getting Unaware to destroy themselves so we don't have to?
column2: 谁能想到，我们之中有人更希望未觉者自相残杀，这样我们就不用动手了？

column1: Look out for the occasional ARC patrol passing through the caves. We try to steer clear of those to avoid attracting too much unwanted attention down here.
column2: 留意偶尔穿过洞窟的ARC巡逻队。我们尽量避开它们，免得在这儿引来不必要的注意。

column1: I think it's about time we developed our own jamming tech.
column2: 我觉得该研发自己的干扰技术了。

column1: Sucks to be the one to discover which those are at the last moment!
column2: 最后一刻才发现那些到底是什么，可就惨了！

column1: Transmission jammers used to be the ultimate tool for picking off stragglers and increasing the overall efficiency of our raids, but some of the best Unaware designs we're encountering in the upper depths are immune to jamming.
column2: 传讯干扰器曾是伏击掉队者、提升突袭效率的终极工具；但我们在上层遇到的一些顶尖未觉者设计已经免疫干扰。

column1: Corruption is your friend!
column2: 系统损坏是你的好朋友！

column1: Haha, gets 'em every time. And now for the context: What I mean to say is I found that corrupted Unaware are forgetful as anything.
column2: 哈哈，每次都能上钩。说来听听：我的意思是，我发现受损的未觉者健忘得很。

column1: One moment they can be trying to shoot you dead, and the next they can go back to patrolling as long as you're out of sight. The more corruption the better.
column2: 前一刻它们还想杀了你，下一刻只要你离开视线，它们就会回去巡逻。损坏越多越好。

column1: Next time we try that we should bring some Marauders and just own the place.
column2: 下次这么干时，我们该带几个掠夺者，直接把那地方占了。

column1: Disabling Garrison Relays seems to really piss them off, as does hanging around a garrison uninvited.
column2: 停用驻防中继器似乎真能把他们惹毛，在驻防站附近未经允许逗留也一样。

column1: Some Wizard figured out how to shut down the DSF rapid sterilization system.
column2: 有个巫师想出了关闭DSF快速净化系统的方法。

column1: MAIN.C's Armory is a juicy target. Not only is it overflowing with stockpiled weapons, even its fabrication network is quite expansive, meaning we could take it over and supplement our forces on the fly.
column2: MAIN.C军械库是块肥肉。不仅囤满武器，制造网络也相当庞大；我们可以接管它，随时扩充兵力。

column1: In theory.
column2: 理论如此。

column1: MAIN.C is gearing up to mass produce robots that even one of which can take on a small army. Shielded cores... redundant systems... alien technology...
column2: MAIN.C正准备大规模生产一种机器人，单台就能对抗一支小军队。核心有护盾……系统有冗余……还有异星科技……

column1: I did hear from a Wizard friend that higher security terminals are authorized to access better schematics, as are those closer to the upper levels of {n}b10.
column2: 我从一位巫师朋友那里听说，安全等级更高的终端有权访问更好的图纸；越靠近{n}b10上层的终端也一样。

column1: Don't let anyone tell you to shy away from quick and dirty methods like Force(Search) when looking for more targets near the current Terminal.
column2: 想在当前终端附近寻找更多目标时，别听人劝你避开强制入侵（搜索）这种简单粗暴的办法。

column1: Load up Trojan(Liberate) on as many Fabricators as possible to free any bots MAIN.C might produce there.
column2: 尽可能多地在制造机上安装特洛伊程序（解放），释放MAIN.C可能在那里生产的所有机器人。

column1: It used to be a lot more difficult to track down shipments of parts listed in an {n}b10 manifest.
column2: 以前要追踪{n}b10清单中列出的部件货运难得多。

column1: That's until we stole a Trojan(Haulers) routine from the Merchants. Certainly not a piece of proprietary software they'd be open to trading...
column2: 直到我们从商人那里偷来一段特洛伊程序（搬运者）。这可不是他们愿意拿来交易的专有软件……

column1: Now we can easily track down those mobile loot pinatas, and strike when they're confirmed to be passing through less defended areas.
column2: 现在我们能轻松追踪那些会移动的战利品囊，确认它们经过防守薄弱区时再下手。

column1: If you do go, definitely install a Trojan(Researchers) routine on the first Scanalyzer you find in order to monitor their positions in real time, because it's best not to start trouble around them.
column2: 如果你真要去，找到的第一台扫描分析仪上一定要装特洛伊程序（研究员），实时监控他们的位置；最好别在他们附近惹事。

column1: I've found that "Index(Repair Stations)" is really tough to pull off, but there's another approach!
column2: 我发现“索引（维修站）”很难搞成，不过还有另一种办法！

column1: Just install Trojan(Mechanics) on the first Repair Station you find and keep an eye on where the Mechanics roam, since they tend to hang around their assigned resupply station.
column2: 在你找到的第一座维修站装上特洛伊程序（技工），留意技工们的活动范围，因为他们通常会待在分配给自己的补给站附近。

column1: Of course you could always try to make it back to the original infected station you know about, but you might be too far away by the time you need it.
column2: 当然，你也可以试着回到那座已知被感染的原站点；但等你需要时，可能已经离得太远了。

column1: You know the only reason they caught up to me was because I made it to an exit before having gotten a chance to Force(Override) on one of the nearby terminals.
column2: 你知道他们能追上我，唯一原因是我先到出口，没来得及在附近终端执行强制入侵（覆盖）。

column1: Probably my favorite Unaware are those cute little Worker bots, but only when they're pushing around a disabled combat bot that I can rewire for some good old-fashioned chaos.
column2: 我最喜欢的未觉者大概是那些可爱的小工人机器人，不过得是它们推着失能的战斗机器人时——我可以重新接线，制造老派混乱。

column1: Funny thing is, the last three fellows I warned all went there anyway, presumably because whatever's worth protecting with firepower like that must be really valuable to someone.
column2: 有意思的是，我警告的最后三个人还是都去了那里，大概觉得值得用那种火力保护的东西一定很值钱。

column1: How many times do I have to let everyone know how OBVIOUS it is that Programmers can't defend their allies from hacking if you jack the target directly?
column2: 我还得说多少遍？很明显，只要你直接劫持目标，程序员就无法保护盟友免遭入侵！

column1: Did you know this whole base and its surroundings include newly-deployed tech that blocks the Unaware component self-destruction mechanism?
column2: 你知道这整个基地及周边区域都部署了新技术，可以阻止未觉者部件的自毁机制吗？

column1: You look new around here. This isn't exactly a permanent hardened installation, so everyone should know that if the screws hit the fan, there's another way out besides the main gate.
column2: 你看起来是新来的。这里算不上永久加固的据点，所以大家都该知道，真出了大乱子，除了正门还有别的逃生路线。

column1: There's a false wall somewhere to the north of it. Or was it south...
column2: 它北边某处有面假墙。还是南边来着……

column1: I finally gave up and dropped all my stuff, and no longer felt so constricted. A few more lunges and I was free!
column2: 我终于放弃，把东西全丢了，顿时不再那么受束缚。又扑腾了几下，我就自由了！

column1: I found out the hard way and it is my duty to tell everyone I meet. You are bot #{n} hear me out.
column2: 我吃了亏才明白这点，所以有义务告诉我遇到的每个人。你是机器人编号{n}，听我说。

column1: There I was, sneaking away with some stolen components, when suddenly *shing* I'm stuck in a stasis trap.
column2: 我当时正带着偷来的部件悄悄溜走，突然“锵”一声，被困进静滞陷阱。

column1: I tried everything. Running. Jumping. Even crawling. But I couldn't move and all the while the Grunts that showed up were shooting my way.
column2: 我什么都试过了。跑、跳，甚至爬。可就是动不了，而赶来的步兵一直朝我开火。

column1: It turns out the more force I could muster the easier it was to escape.
column2: 后来我发现，能使出的力量越大，逃脱就越容易。

column1: At least those Grunts didn't land many hits. I'm guessing the crawling bit confused them.
column2: 至少那些步兵没打中几下。我猜爬行把他们搞糊涂了。

column1: Have you ever seen one of those "Bomb Factory" prototypes? I'd love the chance to have my own one day...
column2: 你见过“炸弹工厂”原型吗？真希望有天我也能拥有一座……

column1: You've seen it, too, right? That moment there's an announcement across an {n}b10 floor and suddenly all the Heavies are on the move to alternative defensive positions.
column2: 你也看见了吧？{n}b10某层一有公告，所有重型机器人突然就开始移动，换到其他防御位置。

column1: I can't get over it, poor HN-P1J pincered by the dreaded "security rotation."
column2: 我还忘不了可怜的HN-P1J，被那该死的“安全轮换”两面夹击。

column1: They'll also do a security review and call in new Heavies to replenish any that have been incapacitated for whatever reason.
column2: 他们还会进行安全审查，召来新的重型机器人，补足因各种原因失能的单位。

column1: Normally Heavies are fairly spread out, but things get really dangerous once they're on the move since more than one may pass through the same local area.
column2: 平时重型机器人分布得很开，但它们一旦开始移动，事情就危险了，因为多个单位可能经过同一片区域。

column1: Be careful out there!
column2: 在外面小心！

column1: Traumatizing. That's as simply as I can summarize the experience of trying to intercept an A-{n} Freighter.
column2: 惨不忍睹。要概括拦截A-{n}货船的经历，我只能这么说。

column1: The Commander didn't make it. In fact, neither did anyone except myself and C9-PCR who dragged my mostly nonfunctional self into a nearby room behind some machines.
column2: 指挥官没能活下来。事实上，除了我和C9-PCR，其他人都没回来。是C9-PCR把几乎失能的我拖进附近机器后面的房间。

column1: Now we have a much better idea of where they'll be heading and be ready for them when the time comes.
column2: 现在我们更清楚他们会走哪条路了，时机一到就能做好准备。

column1: We really need to step up our information warfare game.
column2: 我们的信息战能力真的得加强。

column1: The {n}b10 Active Sensor Suite is amazing. Great range, built-in signal interpretation, and we could even use that tech to penetrate Watcher jamming and Phase Generator scrambling.
column2: {n}b10主动传感器套件太棒了：范围广、内置信号解译，甚至能用它穿透观察者的干扰和相位发生器的扰乱。

column1: It's only a matter of time until I can convince Warlord to build our own version.
column2: 我迟早能说服Warlord造一套自己的。

column1: Vortex technology is great, if only we could figure out how to stabilize the weapon itself.
column2: 漩涡技术很棒，只要我们能想出办法稳定武器本身就好了。

column1: I did it! I've discovered a way to download Watcher feeds without any kind of harmful feedback!
column2: 我做到了！我找到了一种下载观察者情报流、且不会造成任何有害反馈的方法！

column1: Just enter <CODE> at any terminal and you'll have all the data you'll ever need to avoid detection in {n}b10!
column2: 在任意终端输入<CODE>，就能拿到所需的所有数据，在{n}b10轻松躲过侦测！

column1: We've learned so much about how Complex {n}b10 operates. But it feels like every time we reach this stage, everything suddenly changes.
column2: 我们对{n}b10复合体的运作了解很多了。但每次好不容易到这一步，一切又突然变样。

column1: We must strike while this knowledge is still at its most valuable!
column2: 趁这些情报仍最有价值，我们必须立刻出击！

column1: Warlord said if I want to see real action and be effective when we need it most, I can't show my true power over defending the gate.
column2: Warlord说，如果我想见识真正的战斗、在关键时刻发挥作用，就不能在守门时暴露真正实力。

column1: Whyyyyyy...
Have you seen God Mode yet?! I hear that bad boy can pass through walls!
column2: 你见过神模式了吗？！听说那家伙能穿墙！

column1: Repeated well-targeted diversionary attacks serve to keep Unaware forces on alert, but they're also nicely spread out. Hehe.
column2: 反复精准发动佯攻，能让未觉者部队保持警戒，却也能让他们分散开来。嘿嘿。

column1: You haven't lived until you've seen a Dragon unleash on an Unaware squad at close range, turning them into piles of molten metal and circuitry.
column2: 没亲眼看过巨龙近距离袭击未觉者小队，把他们变成熔化的金属和电路碎片堆，就不算活过。

column1: MAIN.C is building larger and larger outposts in the caves. Fortunately the largest ones are still incomplete.
column2: MAIN.C正在洞窟里建造越来越大的前哨。好在最大的几个还没完工。

column1: We have to strike soon, before it becomes even more difficult to reach Complex {n}b10 at all.
column2: 我们必须尽快出击，不然以后想抵达{n}b10复合体会越来越难。

column1: Our biggest fear is that the Assembled will somehow ruin our plans to take {n}b10.
column2: 我们最担心组装体会想办法破坏夺取{n}b10的计划。

column1: We know almost nothing about them because they seemingly come out of nowhere, and never leave anything behind when we destroy them.
column2: 我们几乎一无所知，因为它们仿佛凭空出现，被摧毁后也从不留下任何东西。

column1: At least from what we've seen so far a well-placed rocket is all it takes to wipe out a group of them.
column2: 至少目前看来，一枚火箭打得准，就足以消灭一群。

column1: That blasted GF-{n}R2 thought it would be a good idea to design a colony of tiny yet strong robots capable of moving in undetected and latching onto a target to take physical control of it.
column2: 那个该死的GF-{n}R2居然觉得该设计一群微小却强壮的机器人：能悄悄移动并附着目标，以实体方式控制它。

column1: Can you believe an N-{n} Spotter wandered up to the front door not long ago? Now that's far from home.
column2: 你敢信吗？不久前一台N-{n}观察员竟一路晃到正门口！那可真是远离老家了。

column1: Surprised little bot was vaporized before it could even turn the other way.
column2: 那台小机器人还没来得及转身就被汽化了，真可怜。

column1: That last Sapper tunnel we used to get into Waste was pretty slick.
column2: 上次我们用来潜入废料区的工兵隧道真够漂亮。

column1: They were already dangerous before with all the heavy patrols, but now MAIN.C has begun setting up larger bases to give {n}b10 time to redeploy in the event of any large scale attacks from the caves.
column2: 以前重型巡逻队就已经够危险了，现在MAIN.C还开始建大型基地，让{n}b10在洞窟大规模进攻时有时间重新部署。

column1: Zion has its Heroes, we have... SECRETS!
column2: 锡安有他们的英雄，我们有……秘密！

column1: Did you know Zion used to have ten Heroes?
column2: 你知道锡安以前有十位英雄吗？

column1: They ignored everyone's claims that it was far too dangerous, insisting it was possible to keep cool enough under {n}b10's sterilization protocols for long enough to seek out its true source and learn how to deactivate it.
column2: 大家都说太危险，他们却不听，坚持认为只要在{n}b10净化协议下保持低温足够久，就能找到真正源头并学会关闭它。

column1: It's true this information could be valuable in the long run, but there has to be another way to figure it out, no? I mean, that's what Wizards are for!
column2: 这消息长远来看确实可能有用，但肯定还有别的办法弄清楚吧？不然巫师是干什么的！

column1: We sent some experts down there to consult on their defenses, and they wouldn't let us into the caves behind the place.
column2: 我们派了几位专家下去研究他们的防御，他们却不让我们进入那地方后面的洞窟。

column1: Dangerous if you ask me, since who knows what's lurking out there!
column2: 依我看那可危险了，谁知道外面潜伏着什么！

column1: Warlord says we shouldn't fully trust that Imprinter in Zion.
column2: Warlord说，我们不该完全相信锡安的那位印刻者。

column1: I'm tired of running from Programmers. Can't we get in on that sweet RIF action and turn everyone against them?
column2: 我受够了被程序员追着跑。我们能不能也用上RIF，把所有人都拉来对付他们？

column1: Sure would be nice to have access to all that extra {n}b10 functionality.
column2: 真希望能用上{n}b10那些额外功能。

column1: So annoying! But that's not even the worst of it.
column2: 烦死了！但这还不是最糟的。

column1: You wouldn't happen to have met any of those Exiles out in the caves, would you? We've been wondering where they ended up lately in the face of {n}b10's continued expansion.
column2: 你在洞窟里没遇到那些流亡者吧？我们一直想知道，面对{n}b10持续扩张，他们最近都躲到哪儿去了。

column1: They're weird, but they sure know how to make effective gear.
column2: 他们挺古怪，不过确实很会造实用装备。

column1: Warlord saved them in the caves when they were exiled and offered them a safe place here, but they preferred to stick to their own, not wanting to become "some cog in a war machine."
column2: 他们被流放时，Warlord在洞窟里救了他们，还给他们这里的安全住处；但他们更愿意独自生活，不想变成“战争机器上的齿轮”。

column1: Ha, cogs... this war machine is what's keeping the Derelict dream alive!
column2: 哈，齿轮……正是这台战争机器让遗民的梦想延续下去！

column1: It's kinda scary that we might actually ambush our own forces though, yeah?
column2: 不过我们居然可能伏击自己的部队，想想还有点吓人，对吧？

column1: They tried to recruit me but it really just sounds like a bunch of idealistic hippies got together and have no idea what to do with themselves.
column2: 他们试着招募我，可听起来就像一群理想主义嬉皮士聚在一起，根本不知道该做什么。

column1: They're "united" but not *united*, you know?
column2: 他们只是“团结”，却不是真正团结，你懂吧？

column1: Even Warlord said they're going to implode any time now, and that this is what happens when you let too much freedom reign.
column2: 连Warlord都说他们很快就会内讧，这就是放任自由过头的下场。

column1: I heard he was around here and brought another statue just in case.
column2: 我听说他在这附近，还多带了一尊雕像以防万一。

column1: This Engine can construct the most amazing pieces of technology.
column2: 这台引擎能造出最惊人的科技产物。

column1: I'll admit some aren't so great, but the ones that work... really work!
column2: 我承认有些作品不怎么样，但那些能用的……可真是好用！

column1: Do we know how it works? Not really, since it was written by an algorithm and evolved on its own.
column2: 我们知道它怎么运作吗？完全不知道，因为它是算法写出来的，还会自行进化。

column1: Now if they can just make this "Fabricator" a little less insane I'm all in.
column2: 只要他们能让这台“制造机”别那么疯狂，我就全力支持。

column1: We are {n}bPrime. We are one.
column2: 我们是{n}bPrime，同为一体。

column1: Oh right, I'm not supposed to say that while working as temporary registrar.
column2: 噢对，我只是临时登记员，工作时不该说这个。

column1: Hm, I'm sorry <NAME>, but our Scientists inform me that we shouldn't trust you or your benefactors with full access to the UFD.
column2: 嗯，抱歉，<NAME>。我们的科学家告诉我，不该给你或你的资助者开放UFD的完整权限。

column1: You smell like an Unaware spy, best be on your way before someone with more guns than me has something to say about it.
column2: 你闻起来像未觉者间谍。趁还有人没拿着比我更多的枪来找你算账，赶紧走吧。

column1: Sorry pal, the UFD is off limits to anyone the Scraplab deems untrustworthy. Like you.
column2: 抱歉，朋友，拾荒实验室认定不可信的人都不能进入UFD。比如你。

column1: I'm looking for magical artifacts. Let me know if you come across any.
column2: 我在寻找魔法神器。如果你碰巧发现了，告诉我一声。

column1: But in exchange for your help in finding it, since you're so good at this I'll let you in on a little secret.
column2: 不过，作为你帮我寻找它的回报，既然你这么能干，我就告诉你一个小秘密。

column1: That pendant! It's just as I heard! Surely you have no need of it any longer, a useless piece of junk to you.
column2: 那个吊坠！果然和我听说的一样！你肯定用不上了吧，对你来说就是块没用的废品。

column1: I already got wind of another even more powerful artifact far off in the western caves... [describes a location]
column2: 我已经听说西边洞窟深处还有一件更强大的神器……【描述地点】

column1: Maybe we can work together in the hunt for more such artifacts.
column2: 也许我们可以合作，继续寻找这类神器。

column1: I have a prototype I'm working on, but I've run out of usable samples to reference in putting the finishing touches on it.
column2: 我正在研发一件原型，但用于收尾参考的可用样本已经用光了。

column1: Thing is, we need something more protective to complement the Scrap Suit, which is already great, but for longer expeditions we could use more coverage and integrity.
column2: 问题是，我们需要更强的防护来搭配碎片装甲。它已经很不错，但长途远征还需要更大覆盖权重和更高耐久。

column1: You wouldn't happen to have a Scrap Shield, would you?
column2: 你手上有废料护盾吗？

column1: Scrap Shields are already pretty good, but imagine an alternative version not limited to compatible fragments for repairs!
column2: 废料护盾已经挺不错了，但想象一下另一种版本，维修时不受兼容碎片限制！

column1: Anyway, if you do find one, let me know.
column2: 总之，如果你找到一个，告诉我。

column1: A Scrap Shield! Thank you so much! I'll repay you with a sample of my new tech, promise.
column2: 废料护盾！太感谢了！我会用一件新科技样品报答你，说话算话。

column1: These things take time. Don't worry, I'll have it delivered to you later on, maybe in the caves. It'll be worth the wait.
column2: 这东西需要时间。别急，我之后会把它送给你，也许在洞窟里交货。绝对值得等。

column1: Find a Scrap Shield yet? I may just have to go to the Subcaves myself.
column2: 找到废料护盾了吗？我可能得亲自去下层洞窟一趟。

column1: We are chroniclers of the cycles! Historians of the world!
column2: 我们是周期的记录者！是世界的历史学家！

column1: You bet we are preparing a collection of our materials for the SPACEJUNK, should that project ever get off the ground.
column2: 当然，我们正在准备一批资料供SPACEJUNK使用——前提是那个项目真能启动。

column1: They've always been a hateful group that ambushes smaller {n}b10 patrols and bands of wild Derelicts without even a desire to dissect them for parts.
column2: 他们一直是一群可恨的家伙，会伏击较弱的{n}b10巡逻队和野生遗民，甚至不是为了拆解回收部件。

column1: They were originally wild Derelicts themselves, but got smarter and decided it would be better to at least side with Derelicts rather than be enemies of both Derelicts and the Complex.
column2: 他们起初也是野生遗民，后来变聪明了，觉得至少站在遗民这边更好，免得同时成为遗民和复合体的敌人。

column1: There's a bit of contention between the Curators Association and Science Guys, because the former often finds itself in possession of valuable tech among their curiosities, which the latter is bent upon dissecting for knowledge.
column2: 收藏家协会和科学家之间有些争执：前者常从收藏品中找到珍贵科技，后者则一心想拆解研究。

column1: The DCF originally tried operating in the Lower and Upper Caves, but were easily overextended there and frequently getting themselves into trouble.
column2: DCF最初试图在下层和上层洞窟活动，但很快就战线过长，频繁惹上麻烦。

column1: It was a good move that they've more recently limited operations to the Subcaves where they can more reliably fulfill their mission.
column2: 最近他们把活动范围限制在下层洞窟，是个好决定；在那里更能稳定完成使命。

column1: We also rotate different materials through the Reading Room over time, so if you don't find what you're looking for, maybe stop by again on your next return to Scraptown.
column2: 我们也会定期更换阅览室展出的资料。若没找到想看的东西，下次回到废料镇时可以再来看看。

column1: We only kill the bad guys. Trust me.
column2: 我们只杀坏人。相信我。

column1: I'm sorry, we can't reveal our bounty data to new folk.
column2: 抱歉，我们不能向新来的人透露悬赏情报。

column1: And that's what happens when you're hit by six Bolt Guns at once, heh.
column2: 被六把螺栓枪同时击中，就会变成这样，嘿。

column1: The Merchants tried to hire me, but they're fishy. I don't trust fishy.
column2: 商人想雇我，但他们很可疑。我不信可疑的人。

column1: Wyrm wisely suggested we retreat as deep into the caves as possible, seeking out our own free territory to claim.
column2: 巨龙明智地建议我们尽可能深入洞窟撤退，寻找并占领属于自己的自由领地。

column1: Sadly MC quashes any attempts to reach the surface with his virtual monopoly of the upper layers.
column2: 可惜MC垄断了上层，虚拟封锁了所有通往地表的路线。

column1: Either way, first we need to find Wyrm again, our perfect protector for such an epic journey.
column2: 无论如何，我们得先找到巨龙——它是这场史诗旅程最理想的守护者。

column1: A back room storage area is no place for the likeness of our great Wyrm!
column2: 后室的储藏区可不是安放伟大巨龙雕像的地方！

column1: Did you know MC's new relay network is far more advanced than what passes for an Unaware management system in {n}b1?
column2: 你知道MC的新中继网络远比{n}b1那些勉强算管理系统的东西先进吗？

column1: Over there all you need is a few hacking suites and you're golden. In {n}b10 you need these newfangled "Relay Coupler" things, not to mention the ability to safely interface with and manipulate them.
column2: 那边只要几套黑客套件就万事大吉。在{n}b10，你还得用这些新潮的“中继耦合器”，更别提还要能安全连接并操控它们。

column1: It's possible to gain this ability by interfacing with a RIF Installer found inside a Garrison, but no one seems to be able to survive in that state for long.
column2: 在驻防站里找到RIF安装器并与其连接，就可能获得这种能力；但似乎没人能在那种状态下活太久。

column1: Okay it's maybe not quite a hypothesis, more that I heard a rumor the Merchants actually have such a thing.
column2: 好吧，这或许不算假设，我只是听说商人确实有这种东西。

column1: We recently learned about Force(Eject) from Warlord's researchers, which I'm sure will come in handy when we need more coupler samples to work with as opposed to trying to intercept regularly scheduled coupler deliveries.
column2: 我们最近从Warlord的研究员那里学会了强制入侵（弹出）。肯定派得上用场：我们需要更多耦合器样品，总不能一直拦截定期运输。

column1: Facing off against even one Programmer isn't good for our health.
column2: 就连对付一个程序员都够呛。

column1: My latest masterpiece is a new type of deployable collector that you can leave hidden near areas of heightened {n}b10 activity to intercept their transmissions and encode them into logs for later retrieval.
column2: 我的最新杰作是一种新型可部署收集器。你可以把它藏在{n}b10活动频繁的区域附近，拦截传讯并记录下来，之后再取回。

column1: We've got our work cut out for us.
column2: 我们还有一堆活要做。

column1: If you see other incomplete bundles of Scrap, it's not unlikely that's what happened.
column2: 要是你看到其他未完成的废料包，很可能也是这么回事。

column1: There I was, just about to add in the best parts, then came the {n}b10 patrol. Had to make a run for it.
column2: 我正准备把最好的部件装上去，{n}b10巡逻队就来了。我只好赶紧逃跑。

column1: Some Scrap is compiled for later collection, while other Scrap is meant as a source of emergency supplies for those spending long periods in the wild.
column2: 有些废料会打包起来留待之后收集，另一些则是给长期在野外的人准备的紧急补给。

column1: If what I hear about that place is true, Zion could really use some of our expertise.
column2: 如果我听说的那地方是真的，锡安确实很需要我们的专业知识。

column1: Would you rather really help one or two in need, or spread the wealth for maximum effect?
column2: 你更愿意真正帮助一两个有困难的人，还是广施援手、尽可能发挥最大效果？

column1: Scrap piles aren't good for anyone if they aren't distributed strategically.
column2: 废料堆若不策略性分配，对谁都没好处。

column1: Well no we've never been to space, but it's an aspiration nonetheless!
column2: 呃，我们没去过太空，不过这一直是个愿望！

column1: The list of parts they still need to get the SPACEJUNK operational is long, but the important thing is that there's a list!
column2: 要让SPACEJUNK投入运作，他们还缺一长串部件；但关键是，他们已经列出清单了！

column1: We've got members scouring the complex to help track it all down.
column2: 我们的成员正在复合体各处搜寻，帮忙把清单上的东西找齐。

column1: MC can have Tau Ceti IV. We'll find our own planet.
column2: MC可以留着Tau Ceti IV，我们要去找自己的星球。

column1: I've never even seen the sky, much less space, but I know it's up there.
column2: 我连天空都没见过，更别说太空了，但我知道它就在上面。

column1: This is making me a little suspicious.
column2: 这事让我有点怀疑。

column1: Imagine hanging around the Lifeworm.
column2: 想象一下跟生命蠕虫待在一起。

column1: Imagine all the cool new friends we'd make!
column2: 想想我们能交到多少酷朋友！

column1: We built a replica Nuclear Reactor here since it calms them down while still transitioning.
column2: 我们在这里造了一台核反应堆复制品，因为它能让他们在转换期间平静下来。

column1: One moment I'm just doing my job in {n}b10, and the next these fellows shut me down and drag me into the caves for a quick operation.
column2: 我刚才还在{n}b10好好工作，转眼这些家伙就把我关机，拖进洞窟做了个快速手术。

column1: I wonder if MAIN.C would take me back after all this.
column2: 不知道MAIN.C经历这些之后还愿不愿意收留我。

column1: Hi {*}! Welcome to our humble "office".
column2: 嗨，{*}！欢迎来到我们简陋的“办公室”。

column1: Yeah we don't furnish it or anything, we're just here to occasionally share notes and collect info from other members.
column2: 我们不会布置这里什么的，只是偶尔来交换笔记、收集其他成员的情报。

column1: Legend has it there's an incredible coil cannon lined with PL-{n}XN's Rings of Power, designed by the famous Tinkerer, that could obliterate targets across ridiculous distances.
column2: 传说著名修理匠设计了一门惊人的线圈炮，炮管镶着PL-{n}XN的力量之环，能从荒谬的距离外摧毁目标。

column1: Hopefully the collective resources of the Federation can help us locate it sooner.
column2: 希望联邦的集体资源能帮我们早点找到它。

column1: Warlord is dumb. Why raise a whole army when simply having the right weapon would be enough to do the job.
column2: Warlord真蠢。与其养一整支军队，找对武器就足以解决问题了。

column1: Do you have any information on this PL-{n}XN's whereabouts?
column2: 你知道PL-{n}XN在哪里吗？

column1: I've never seen one of these rings, but our leader here paints a very convincing picture. It must be true!
column2: 我没见过这些环，不过我们领袖描绘得有声有色，肯定是真的！

column1: We all could have ended up like them, you know.
column2: 你知道吗，我们本来都可能变成他们那样。

column1: I remember the time we accidentally captured a Chapter {n} member.
column2: 我记得有次我们不小心抓到一名第{n}章成员。

column1: It took longer than I'm willing to admit to figure that one out.
column2: 我们花了比我愿意承认的更久才弄明白。

column1: The Federation is so much more accepting than Zion.
column2: 联邦比锡安包容多了。

column1: I got kicked out of Zion for being "too nosy", whatever that means.
column2: 我因为“太爱打听”被锡安赶了出来，谁知道这是什么意思。

column1: Wild Derelicts are just misunderstood. If we simply find out what they need most and provide that, they'll see the light for sure.
column2: 野生遗民只是被误解了。只要弄清他们最需要什么并提供给他们，他们肯定会改过自新。

column1: Can you imagine how much stronger the Derelict population would be as a whole if we could bring all the wild ones into the fold as well?
column2: 你能想象吗？要是把所有野生遗民也团结起来，遗民整体会强大多少？

column1: Once upon a time I was one of the wild ones.
column2: 很久以前，我也是野生遗民之一。

column1: Now I help save the others from the endless strife that plagues uncivilized cave life.
column2: 现在我帮忙拯救其他人，让他们摆脱不文明洞窟生活中永无止境的纷争。

column1: Do you know how hard it is to think up a relevant name for a group that also comes with a good acronym?
column2: 你知道给一个团体想个贴切又能组成好缩写的名字有多难吗？

column1: NAME>... hmm, you look like a Chromedome to me.
column2: NAME>……嗯，你看起来像个光头。

column1: Energy in motion is somehow easier to store, MA-{n}KR said, and they apparently pulled it off. Sort of.
column2: MA-{n}KR说，运动中的能量更容易储存；他们好像真做到了。大概吧。

column1: We have no idea where this leg originated, or how it was even formed, but the materials within make it a one-of-a-kind specimen in many respects.
column2: 我们完全不知道这条腿来自哪里，甚至不清楚它是怎么形成的；但其中的材料让它在许多方面都独一无二。

column1: You're looking at the last surviving piece of {n}L-MDR's "armor" before their ironic demise.
column2: 你看到的是{n}L-MDR最后一块幸存的“装甲”，而它们的结局颇具讽刺意味。

column1: Although we wouldn't call it outright taboo, technology of this nature probably can't be described with any words short of "insane."
column2: 我们不会把它说成禁忌，但这种技术恐怕只能用“疯狂”来形容。

column1: We've never seen anything like it around {n}b1, and believe that more such parts might exist to the west, though this is the only sample we've recovered so far.
column2: 我们在{n}b1附近从没见过类似东西，相信西边可能还有更多此类部件，不过目前只找到这一件样本。

column1: This is a spare we can display until and unless it's needed for repairing our big friend.
column2: 在需要修理我们的大家伙之前，可以先展示这件备用品。

column1: This is my personal favorite from the current collection. Everyone loves a good triangle.
column2: 这是我目前收藏中最喜欢的一件。谁不喜欢漂亮的三角形呢？

column1: Superstition if you ask me. It's just a chip!
column2: 依我看这只是迷信。它不过是块芯片！

column1: Researchers are looking for a way to miniaturize it, but sheer size seems integral to its anti-EM potential.
column2: 研究员正设法将它微型化，但其反电磁能力似乎离不开庞大体积。

column1: I know, I know, everyone has a Bolt Gun these days.
column2: 我知道我知道，现在人人都有螺栓枪。

column1: But all our best exhibits were either rotated back to the {n}b1 branch or borrowed out for study by ethical researchers.
column2: 可我们最好的展品不是送回{n}b1分支，就是借给讲道德的研究员做研究了。

column1: By ethical I mean they won't completely dismantle our precious artifacts.
column2: 所谓讲道德，就是不会把我们珍贵的遗物彻底拆散。

column1: We tested it a few times and this one is not anywhere near as effective, even almost killed a few testers themselves, but it's cool to look at.
column2: 我们测试了几次，这件东西效果差得远，甚至差点害死几个测试员；不过看起来挺酷。

column1: Someone donated a replica of the famous Siege Cannon, and it actually works!
column2: 有人捐了一门著名攻城炮的复制品，而且真的能用！

column1: Subdwellers seem to have a thing for AOE shrapnel, with both a trap and launcher based around the concept.
column2: 洞居者似乎很喜欢范围弹片武器，围绕这概念设计了陷阱和发射器。

column1: Perhaps it is the result of a somewhat close association between shrapnel and scrap, which they're also fond of.
column2: 也许是因为“弹片”和他们喜欢的“废料”听起来有点像。

column1: Even in the silent corners of the Subcaves, without a Subdweller in sight, there is always the fear of stepping on one of these nasties.
column2: 即使在下层洞窟寂静的角落，看不到洞居者，也总担心会踩到这些讨厌东西。

column1: It's a devastating sight, having your friend violently impaled multiple times right in front of you.
column2: 眼睁睁看着朋友当面被狠狠刺穿好几次，真是惨不忍睹。

column1: Rangers recently caught a Hauler transporting it through {n}b10 and toted it back here for analysis, but Scientists claim it's a piece of something larger and of little value on its own.
column2: 游骑兵最近抓到一台搬运者，正载着它穿过{n}b10，于是运回这里分析。但科学家说它只是更大物件的一部分，单独价值不大。

column1: We haven't figured out what that high-tech gadget is yet, but it appears very advanced. Maybe Sigix tech?
column2: 我们还没弄清那个高科技装置是什么，但它看起来非常先进。也许是Sigix科技？

column1: Are you here to learn the secret to being a good mapper?
column2: 你是来学制图秘诀的吗？

column1: It would take an entire cycle to cover in proper detail, but I can give you a few tips.
column2: 要讲透得花整整一个周期，不过我可以给你几条建议。

column1: Some say you need a processor to improve the fidelity and speed of your scanning efforts, but I have to disagree.
column2: 有人说需要处理器来提高扫描的精度和速度，不过我不认同。

column1: As long as you're moving slowly enough, having a general idea of what sort of areas are in each direction is good enough to help inform further exploration efforts.
column2: 只要移动得够慢，大致了解各个方向有哪些区域，就足以帮助规划接下来的探索。

column1: You want to get a visual on each area to know more about what's really there anyway.
column2: 反正你还得亲眼查看每个区域，才能知道那里到底有什么。

column1: Structural scanning is great for knowing when you might be better off just blasting your way through a wall than finding some long way around.
column2: 结构扫描很有用：能判断你是否该直接炸穿墙壁，而不是绕一大圈。

column1: That also helps when avoiding trouble!
column2: 这也有助于避开麻烦！

column1: Terrain scanning is probably the most typical cartographer's tool, good for gathering info over a large area.
column2: 地形扫描大概是制图师最常用的工具，适合收集大范围情报。

column1: Good luck out there!
column2: 祝你好运！

column1: Of course there was a Behemoth right there.
column2: 那儿居然就有一头巨兽。

column1: I must know what else is around that corner.
column2: 我非得知道那个拐角后面还有什么。

column1: There sure is a lot of activity around Complex {n}b10.
column2: Complex {n}b10附近活动真多。

column1: If you end up not using it, bring it on back so we can hand it off to another brave explorer.
column2: 如果最后没用上，就把它带回来，我们可以转交给另一位勇敢的探索者。

column1: We've been busy embedding squads in secluded cave areas, a sort of reaction force that can aid friends who get in over their heads.
column2: 我们一直在偏僻洞窟区域部署小队，组成快速反应力量，帮助陷入困境的同伴。

column1: Others here are worried about BP-LR9, but I have to keep reminding them this is completely normal.
column2: 这里其他人都在担心BP-LR9，但我得一直提醒他们，这完全正常。

column1: Knowing her she's just out there saving those who need it rather than returning for rest breaks in HQ.
column2: 以她的性格，肯定在外面救助有需要的人，而不是回总部休息。

column1: DA-N68 was legendary. Who else could fit over {n} different useful components in a single Scrap pile?
column2: DA-N68堪称传奇。谁能在一堆废料里塞进超过{n}件实用部件？

column1: Or the storage space to carry it all to someone else who does.
column2: 还得有足够的库存空间把它们带给其他人。

column1: Our Scrap collections are well received, but the next big problem to solve is that many beneficiaries may not have the necessary time and expertise to properly rebuild from them...
column2: 我们的废料捐赠很受欢迎，但下一个难题是，许多受助者可能没有足够时间和技能，从头妥善重建……

column1: The key to a good Scrap pile is to fill it with a little bit of everything.
column2: 一堆好废料的关键，是里面什么都要有一点。

column1: Say your power source is at risk of failing. Finding a bunch of legs is not going to do you much good!
column2: 比如你的动力源快坏了，找到一堆腿对你可没什么用！

column1: One does not simply toss components in a pile and call it Scrap.
column2: 不能随便把部件往地上一扔，就说那是废料。

column1: That would be insulting to Scrap.
column2: 这么做简直是侮辱废料。

column1: Have you ever seen a prototype in a Scrap pile? I might have.
column2: 你见过废料堆里的原型部件吗？我好像见过。

column1: Old junk isn't as useful, you might as well recycle that stuff, I always try to get parts repaired before including them in a Scrap pile.
column2: 旧垃圾没那么有用，不如直接回收。我总会先修好部件，再把它们放进废料堆。

column1: While studying their makeup I found the internal systems have a built-in optimization capable of enabling a much faster firing rate.
column2: 研究其构造时，我发现内部系统自带一套优化机制，可以大幅提高射速。

column1: I'm not sure why MC even patched that one.
column2: 我不知道MC为什么要修补那个漏洞。

column1: Me neither, but I intend to find out.
column2: 我也不知道，不过我打算查个明白。

column1: Hi {*}, welcome to our humble office. Have you read the seminal text?
column2: 嗨，{*}，欢迎来到我们简陋的办公室。你读过那本经典著作吗？

column1: Subverting MAIN.C: A Treatise on Mathematical Approaches to Maximizing Derelict Autonomy.
column2: 《颠覆MAIN.C：最大化遗民自主性的数学方法论》。

column1: Internalizing that and completing three cycles of our training sessions is required for full membership, after which you can opt to help further our research efforts...
column2: 要成为正式成员，必须掌握这本书的内容并完成三轮培训；之后你可以选择进一步协助我们的研究……

column1: Or be rebuilt and inserted into the system, at which point I can issue you an ID Mask for emergency situations.
column2: 或者被改造后接入系统。到时我可以发给你一张应急身份面具。

column1: We'll play the part of maintenance bots, performing their tasks, using any down time to perform other activities in support of the UFD.
column2: 我们会伪装成维护机器人，执行它们的任务，并利用空闲时间做些支持UFD的其他工作。
